research_rationale: Executive Order 13755 (81 FR 96329, signed 2016-12-23, published 2016-12-30, FR Doc. 2016-31792) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13755.txt, the registered official original. Number, date, title and signature date match the register. The 23-clause inventory (the opening authority words, Section 1 with items (a) through (p), Section 2(a) through (c), Section 3 and Section 4) covers the whole text. The order is an order of succession under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998 and is not emergency-dependent. Every clause is recorded as continuing on 2026-10-14 because the order has no own-terms end and no held later instrument revokes, supersedes or amends any clause. savings_reason: Executive Order 13755 has no savings or transition clause. The bounded searches found no later instrument that would carry any right or action forward from this order.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13757 (82 FR 1, signed 2016-12-28, published 2017-01-03, FR Doc. 2016-31922) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13757.txt, the registered official original. Number, date, title and signature date match the register. The order is an amending order: it restates section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694, adds the Annex, and adds a new section 10 (delisting authority). The 8-clause inventory (sections 1 through 5, with paragraphs (i), (ii) and (iii) of the restated section 1(a)) covers the whole text. The order depends on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694, which the President continued by notice every year from 2017 through 2026 (ten held notices, recorded as later events on section 1; the last, signed March 24, 2026, runs to April 1, 2027, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14). Two later orders amended the text this order inserted: Executive Order 14144 (2025-01-16) restated it and Executive Order 14306 (2025-06-06) edited two paragraphs. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 these are later events and the clauses continue, amended. Other later orders that mention this order do not revoke or amend any clause of it: Executive Order 13848 states that Executive Order 13694, as amended by this order, remains in effect; Executive Order 13849 recites this order as an earlier additional step under the emergency; Executive Order 14110 (revoked in relevant part by Executive Order 14148, as the March 2025 and March 2026 notices record) and Executive Order 14117 rely on the same emergency; Executive Order 13984 amended section 9 of Executive Order 13694, not a provision this order inserted. The held corpus of executive-order texts runs through Executive Order 14435 (signed 2026-10-05); orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are covered only by the catalog search.
savings_reason: Executive Order 13757 has no savings or transition clause of its own; its section 4 only disclaims private rights. The later amendments restate or edit the blocking criteria without saving or transferring any right or action from the clause as first printed, and the bounded searches found no instrument that would do so.

Each states that Executive Order 14148 revoked Executive Order 14110 in relevant part and continues the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 for one year. Neither revokes, supersedes or amends Executive Order 13757, and each lists it among the orders that took additional steps under the emergency."}

The emergency it depends on was continued every year without a gap through the March 24, 2026 notice. No later order revokes or supersedes it; the amendments by Executive Order 14144 and Executive Order 14306 change the wording of the blocking criteria and are later events, not ends.
scope_check: The order's clauses are the restated blocking provision (section 1 and its paragraphs), the Annex (section 2), the new delisting authority (section 3), the no-rights statement (section 4) and the effective time (section 5). independent_command_check: The delisting authority in section 3, the Annex in section 2 and the blocking command in section 1 are separate commands; none depends on another for its continuation, and none has been ended.

The claim cannot be assembled because the continuation notices are not evidence this packet can cite, and its 113-clause inventory, which includes dated wind-down and effective-date clauses, would still need a clause-by-clause decision.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13848 (83 FR 46843, signed 2018-09-12, published 2018-09-14, FR Doc. 2018-20203) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13848.txt, the registered official original. Number, date, title and signature date match the register. The 54-clause inventory (the opening clause, section 1(a) through (f) with paragraphs (b)(i) and (b)(ii), section 2 with paragraphs (a)(i) through (iii), (b) and (c), section 3 with paragraphs (a) and (b) and the nine listed sanctions, sections 4 through 13, and section 14 with its paragraphs) covers the whole text. The order is emergency-dependent: it declares the national emergency in its opening words, and the President continued the emergency by notice each year from 2019 through 2026 (eight held notices, recorded as later events on the opening clause and on section 2; the last, signed August 31, 2026, continues it beyond September 12, 2026, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14). No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order. The recurring election duties in sections 1 and 3 are not ended by the passing of any election cycle. The only one-time command, the 30-day framework in section 1(f), is a deadline and not an end, and no held source shows its performance. Executive Order 13757 and later orders that amend Executive Order 13694 are not acts on this order; section 2(b) merely states that Executive Order 13694, as amended by Executive Order 13757, remains in effect. The held corpus of executive-order texts runs through Executive Order 14435 (signed 2026-10-05); orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are covered only by the catalog search.
savings_reason: Executive Order 13848 has no savings or transition clause: section 2(c) preserves the prohibitions notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits, and section 14(c) only disclaims private rights. No later instrument acts on the order, so nothing is saved or transferred from it, and the bounded searches found none.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order's text sets no sunset or condition ending it. The national emergency it declared was continued every year from 2019 through the Notice of August 31, 2026 without a gap, and no held instrument revokes or supersedes the order. The 45-day and 30-day periods in section 1 are deadlines and not ends, and the recurring duties are tied to each election, not to a single one.
scope_check: All 54 clauses were read. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. Section 2(b)'s statement about Executive Order 13694 concerns a different order; later amendments to that order do not amend this clause.
independent_command_check: The separate commands are the election assessment and report (section 1(a) through (c)), the 30-day framework (section 1(f)), the blocking of property (section 2), the sanctions review and recommendation (section 3), the donation prohibition (sections 4 and 5), the entry suspension (section 6), the evasion and conspiracy prohibitions (section 7), the no-prior-notice finding (section 9), the implementation authority (section 11) and the reporting authority (section 12). Each continues independently on the same emergency; none has been ended.
